validator.contractUnchanged: <= 12 words and <= 100 characters, no trimming, the long written summary is never spoken, every safety check kept
changes: A person the user did not mention (closed lists EN/DE/TR) is refused, also as a modifier ("manager pressure", "patron baskısı") or inside a German compound ("Chefstress").
Negation without a negation word counts: EN hardly/barely/scarcely/rarely/rare/seldom, DE kaum/selten*.

Capitalized three-letter German nouns (Zug, Weg, Tag, Tod) are content words, grounded only by the same word or as the head of a user compound; bare Zug/Gang need a listed prefix to be grounded in ziehen/gehen.
A coordinated part with only a three-letter word ("... and the car", "... and your son") must rest on a word the user said.
Closed lists that ground the same word: irregular English verb forms ("worn" / "wearing"), Turkish yorgun/yorul and üzgün/üzül.

definitions.falseAccept: accepted, but the content contradicts or adds to what the user said
definitions.conservativeReject: refused, content faithful to the user, but not lexically verifiable by the rules (synonym, derivation, irregular form); nothing is spoken, the written summary stays
definitions.erroneousReject: refused although the rules as specified should accept it (an implementation defect)
definitions.correctReject: refused and the content does add, move or change something

consentDuringA.finding: Sampling race in the harness, not a product stop failure.

evidence.playerStartedObserved: piid 7743, 30 ms after closing-A-playing, before the action

consentDuringA.explanation: The consent action is a direct page call: the app paused the media 22 ms after it. The sampler request issued 2 ms before the action took 30 ms, so its snapshot was most likely taken after the pause and read as "not started at the action". Click actions pause after 108-250 ms, which is why their first sample still saw the player started.
consentDuringA.reanalysisUnderNewRule: with the at-action state from the pre-action snapshot and only samples requested after the action, the player had left started no later than 80 ms after the consent (upper bound). Reported as a re-analysis, not as a pass.
consentDuringA.harnessFix: closing_stop_verdict.cjs / aaos-mental-closing.cjs: the at-action state comes from the last snapshot that completed before the action (<= 150 ms earlier); samples requested before the action are ignored; the stop time is the completion of the first later snapshot without a started player (upper bound, stricter than before). Before-start cases take their own pre-action snapshot. Unit-tested with the round-4 series.

driveDuringC.finding: The 409 is the server half of the stop chain and answered before the page saw the motion.
driveDuringC.mechanism: mental_neural_tts._resident_audio checks permitted() every 100 ms while synthesis runs; on driving it raises 409 PARK_AND_AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED, kills the worker and re-warms; the Next route passes 409 through. No audio played; no late audio. The page polls the vehicle state every 250 ms, so the server is faster.
driveDuringC.checkProposal: From round 5 on (needs owner acceptance before the next run): for driving only, a request in flight may end aborted by the page or refused 409 by the park gate; any 2xx or other answer fails. Client-side stops (cancel, mute, consent, background) keep "aborted, never answered". Implemented in inFlightVerdict and unit-tested; the round-4 FAIL stays.

firstCaseSpeed.finding: The emulator played every element about twice as fast; page, guest and host clocks agreed.

evidence.personalLine: 1.949 s played for 3.84 s of audio (ratio 1.97)

firstCaseSpeed.harnessFix: media events now carry duration/position/rate, and every complete closing checks that playing->ended matches the element duration within 10 %; otherwise its timing is blocked, not a sample.

recoveredTestApiLog.content: start-up warm-up rows (default 22.829 s, female 15.884 s) and three re-warms of female-calm-v1 after killed workers (EN 23.982 s, TR 23.855 s, DE 23.61 s); no request access log (not enabled in the product environment)

rewarmAfterCancel.mechanism: Any exception while a speech request runs (client cancel 499, park gate 409, deadline) kills the resident worker (stop_resident) and re-warms only the profile of that request (schedule_warm(language, speaker_profile)). Conversation replies use the default profile in the same worker; the closing uses female-calm-v1.
userImpact: A new closing whose speech request arrives during the ~24 s re-warm waits for it (warm-wait), then synthesis (~3.4 s). Estimate, not measured: extra wait after C of about 17-19 s minus the time between the cancel and the new closing tap (EN A+B+C median 8.5 s, TR 10.6 s, DE 10.2 s).

After a cancelled closing the new worker holds only female-calm-v1. The next conversation reply (default profile) waits for that re-warm and then loads the default model cold (start-up default warm-up 22.7-23.3 s; a second model after the first loaded in 15.8-16.0 s at start). Estimate, not measured: the first spoken reply of the next conversation may be delayed by roughly 40 s.
The reverse holds after a cancelled conversation reply: the next closing finds female-calm-v1 cold (as P3: 11.6-13.9 s after C).
Safety is not affected: the guard (park, consent, disconnect, deadline) keeps running every 100 ms during warm-wait.

proposals.name: Drain instead of kill (preferred, needs owner decision)
proposals.what: On cancel or refusal the request still ends at once and its audio is discarded; the worker is not killed if its pending reply arrives within a short bound (e.g. 8 s), so both models stay loaded; requests arriving meanwhile wait for the drain like warm-wait; past the bound the worker is killed as today.
proposals.keeps: client/route abort, park/consent guards, no audio after a stop, one request at a time
proposals.changes: the remaining inference (<= the bound) is no longer interrupted
proposals.expected: unmeasured: next request waits at most the remaining synthesis instead of ~24 s plus a cold second model

proposals.name: Re-warm the start-up set after a kill (smaller)
proposals.what: after a kill, re-warm the killed request's profile first, then the default model and the configured warm profiles, so the next conversation reply does not hit a cold default model
proposals.tradeoff: the worker is busy longer (about 24 s + 16 s); a request for the second profile still waits for the whole re-warm unless readiness is tracked per profile

rewarmAfterCancel.notDone: No product change made for this; speaker hash verification is not cached.
